{
 "summary": "Findings: (17 defects: 5 P1, 8 P2, 4 P3. Patch is already applied in the tree; line numbers are for the working files. Read-only review; "probed" means reproduced by running a throwaway bun script against the real modules. The repo has no tests and no stated Design intent beyond the task sentence.)

P1

1. Idempotency key drops legitimate charges and misses real retries
Location: billing.ts:42-46, used at billing.ts:59-61
Failure: Intent Drift (idempotent retry handling). The key is customerId:currency:subtotal:UTC-day and ignores `requestId` (types.ts:17), the only field that identifies a client retry.
- Two different purchases by one customer with the same subtotal on the same day collapse into one: the second is never charged and the caller receives the first entry as if it succeeded. Probed: requestId r1 and r2, both 1000 USD, returned the same entry object.
- Promo is not in the key: r2 carried a 50% promo and still got the full-price entry (gross 1120).
- A retry that crosses UTC midnight gets a new key and double-charges. Probed: same requestId one day later posted a second entry.
- The key is derived from the server clock at processing time, so it is not a property of the request at all.
- The "day bucket keeps the key space from growing" comment is false: `byKey` (ledger.ts:7) is never pruned.
Fix: key on `request.requestId` (scoped by customerId); delete `idempotencyKeyFor` and the day bucket. On a hit, optionally reject when the stored entry's customer/currency/amount differ from the replayed request.

2. Refund returns more than the customer paid (fee applied twice)
Location: billing.ts:88
Failure: `applyProcessingFee(charge.grossCents)` grosses up an amount that already includes the fee (billing.ts:64; types.ts:37 says "processing fee included"). Every refund overpays by 2.9%. Probed: charge gross 1120, refund gross -1152.
Fix: `grossCents: -charge.grossCents`, as the pre-change code did.

3. Refund is converted at today's rate, not the charge's rate
Location: billing.ts:89-90, 97-98
Failure: Conversion timing. The refund reads `this.rates.current()` instead of the rate captured on the charge (`charge.fxRate`, types.ts:41-42). A charge and its full refund no longer net to zero in USD, and the company silently absorbs or gains FX drift. Probed: EUR charge settled 6156; after the rate moved 1.1 to 1.2 the refund settled -6910 (also inflated by finding 2).
Fix: a full reversal posts `settledCents: -charge.settledCents, fxRate: charge.fxRate`. No rate lookup and no `settle` call in `refund`. If the business really wants refund-date FX, that needs an explicit FX gain/loss entry; UNVERIFIED which policy the processor applies.

4. Refunds are not idempotent; a charge can be refunded any number of times
Location: billing.ts:82-103 (key written at billing.ts:100, never read); ledger.ts:13
Failure: Intent Drift (idempotent retry handling). `refund` builds `refund:${charge.id}` but never calls `findByIdempotencyKey`, so a retried refund posts a second negative entry. `Ledger.append` then overwrites the `byKey` slot without complaint. Probed: two `refund()` calls on one charge posted led_3 and led_4, both -1152; `byKey` now points at led_4.
Fix: in `refund`, return the existing entry for `refund:${charge.id}` before appending. Enforce the invariant at its source too: `Ledger.append` throws on a duplicate idempotencyKey instead of overwriting.

5. Reconciliation compares float dollars with `!==` and pages finance spuriously
Location: reconcile.ts:5-11, 17-18
Failure: The total is accumulated as `settledCents / 100` in binary floating point and compared for exact equality. The doc comment itself says the check must never fire spuriously. Probed: entries of 10 and 20 cents against a processor balance of 30 returned a Discrepancy (computed 0.30000000000000004).
Fix: sum integer `settledCents` and compare with `processorBalanceCents`; divide by 100 only for display. Make `Discrepancy` carry `computedCents` (types.ts:54-57 currently mixes cents and dollars in one record).

P2

6. Fixed promo is taxed on the pre-discount amount, percent promo on the post-discount amount
Location: billing.ts:34-36 vs 28-32
Failure: Same economic discount, different total. Probed on subtotal 1000: fixed 500 off gives tax 88, total 588; 50% off gives tax 44, total 544. A fixed promo covering the whole subtotal still bills 88 of tax on a zero-value sale.
Fix: one path: compute `discountCents` per kind, then `discounted = subtotal - discount`, tax on `discounted`. This also removes the three copies of the tax/return logic (Stubborn Duplication; the no-promo branch is just discount 0).

7. Promo values are not validated; negative totals and surcharges are reachable
Location: billing.ts:29, 35; contract at types.ts:11
Failure: `promo` arrives on the ChargeRequest, so it is boundary input. Probed: percent 150 gives discount 1500, tax -44, total -544 (a negative "charge" is posted); fixed -500 gives total 1588 (the promo raises the price); a non-integer fixed value yields fractional cents in the ledger. The percent branch has no cap, although the fixed branch does.
Fix: reject percent outside 0-100 and fixed values that are negative or non-integer, at the top of `computeTotal` (or clamp the discount to 0..subtotal in the single path from finding 6).

8. `settle` rounds from a float major-unit intermediate and misrounds half-cent cases
Location: billing.ts:107-110
Failure: `grossCents / 100 * fxRate * 100` introduces error before `Math.round`. Probed against exact decimal arithmetic: 115 cents at 1.1 gives 126 (exact 126.5 rounds to 127); also 1715, 3305, 3555, 6485, 6735 at 1.1. One cent off per affected entry, which then fails the strict reconciliation.
Fix: keep integers as long as possible: `Math.round(grossCents * fxRate * 100 / minorUnitsPerMajor(currency))`, or better hold rates as scaled integers/decimal strings and round with integer math under an explicit rounding mode.

9. Percent discount and tax rounding go through float products and misround .5 cases
Location: billing.ts:29, 31 (also 25, 34)
Failure: `subtotal * (value / 100)` and `x * 0.0875` are inexact. Probed against exact integer math: discount wrong for 25@58%, 45@70%, 50@29%, 50@57%, 75@82%; tax wrong for 360, 680, 1320, 1400, 2600. Line 29 is new; the tax expression is old but the patch copies it into two more branches. The untouched `applyProcessingFee` (billing.ts:11) has the same defect (1500, 3500, 5500...) and now feeds FX conversion.
Fix: integer arithmetic with rates as basis points: `Math.round(subtotal * value / 100)` and `Math.round(x * 875 / 10000)`; ideally one shared round-half-up helper on integers.

10. Fixed promo "cents" has no currency
Location: types.ts:11-13; billing.ts:35
Failure: A fixed promo is a bare number while the charge can be USD, EUR, GBP, or JPY. A "500" promo is $5.00 on a USD cart and 500 yen (about $3) on a JPY cart; nothing ties the promo to `request.currency`.
Fix: give fixed promos a `currency` and reject a mismatch, or define the value as USD and convert.

11. Replay path keys on time read before the lookup, and a replay silently ignores a changed request
Location: billing.ts:58-61
Failure: `existing` is returned without comparing it to the incoming request, so a client bug that reuses a key for a different amount gets a success with the old amount. Fully resolved by the fix in finding 1 plus a mismatch check; listed separately because it stays true after re-keying on requestId.
Fix: on a hit, compare customerId/currency/recomputed gross and throw on conflict.

12. JPY and other non-cent amounts live in fields named `...Cents`
Location: types.ts:5, 25-28, 38; rates.ts:24-27
Failure: Leaky Interface. `unitCents`, `subtotalCents`, `grossCents` hold whole yen for JPY; correctness depends on every caller remembering `minorUnitsPerMajor`. `formatStatementLine` and reconcile only work because they read `settledCents` (USD).
Fix: rename to `...Minor` (or a `{ amountMinor, currency }` money type) in this change, before more callers exist.

13. No tests for any of the new money paths
Location: repository root (no test files)
Failure: Promo math, FX settlement, replay, refund reversal and reconciliation ship with zero behavioral tests; findings 1-6 would each have been caught by one obvious case.
Fix: add tests for: replay by requestId returns one entry; distinct requests with equal subtotal both post; refund nets charge to zero in both currencies after a rate change; double refund posts once; fixed vs percent tax parity; reconcile of [10, 20] against 30 returns null; JPY settlement.

P3

14. Stored `fxRate` on a refund is the refund-time rate, contradicting the reversal
Location: billing.ts:98; types.ts:41-42
Failure: Parallel State. Disappears with finding 3; noted because the field doc ("captured when the entry posted") would then need to say that refunds inherit the charge's rate.

15. No boundary validation on line items
Location: billing.ts:14-20, 63-77
Failure: Empty `lineItems`, negative or fractional `quantity`/`unitCents` post zero, negative, or fractional-cent charges. `subtotalOf` is old code, but the patch now multiplies its output through discount, FX and reconciliation. A 100% promo also posts a zero-amount charge entry; UNVERIFIED whether that is wanted.
Fix: reject non-integer or negative amounts and empty carts at the top of `charge`.

16. `settle` types its parameter as `LedgerEntry["currency"]`
Location: billing.ts:107
Failure: Indirection for no gain; `Currency` is exported (types.ts:1).
Fix: import and use `Currency`.

17. Statement doc example is misleading
Location: reconcile.ts:24
Failure: The example "led_12  charge  -$10.40" shows a negative charge, which the code only produces from the invalid-promo path in finding 7.
Fix: use a refund in the example.

Not defects: `formatStatementLine` formatting from integer cents is correct. The `BillingService` constructor gained `rates` before `clock`, a breaking positional change, but there are no other callers in this tree.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: 13 defects (5 P1, 6 P2, 2 P3). The change is not safe to merge. Verified = reproduced with a throwaway bun probe against the real api.ts/cache.ts/cursor.ts; the rest are traced from code. The project has only api.ts, cache.ts, cursor.ts, types.ts (patch already applied; no tests, no callers, no AGENTS.md).

## P1

1. Title: Stale tier survives permission invalidation
Severity: P1
Location: cache.ts:72-83 (called from api.ts:83-85)
Failure: Parallel State. `invalidatePrefix` clears `fresh` and `empty` but never `stale`. Any entry already moved to the stale tier (cache.ts:35-36) is still served as `stale` for up to 150 s after access is revoked. Verified: after revoke, the listing returned 10 revoked rows. This is a security boundary failure.
Fix: Also delete matching keys from `stale`. Better: drop the second map and keep one `Map<string, Entry>`, deriving hit/stale/miss from `storedAt`, so there is only one tier to invalidate.

2. Title: In-flight fetch repopulates the cache after invalidation
Severity: P1
Location: api.ts:59-60 and api.ts:67-69
Failure: A miss fetch or background revalidation started before `onPermissionsChanged` stores its pre-revocation rows after the invalidation ran. Those rows are then served as a fresh hit for 30 s plus 120 s stale. Verified: after revoke, 10 rows were served from cache.
Fix: Keep a per-viewer generation counter bumped by `onPermissionsChanged`; capture it before the fetch and skip `store` if it changed.

3. Title: Cache key omits `includeArchived`
Severity: P1
Location: api.ts:7-9
Failure: `Query.includeArchived` (types.ts:36) is passed to the source but is not in the key. For the same viewer, sort, filter, offset and pageSize, an `includeArchived: true` result is served to a later `includeArchived: false` request, and the reverse. Verified: the non-archived request returned the 30 rows cached by the archived request. This leaks archived documents past the "admin-only" flag.
Fix: Add `includeArchived` to the key. Derive the key from every `Query` field so a new field cannot be forgotten.

4. Title: Negative-cache TTL is 5000 s instead of 5 s
Severity: P1
Location: cache.ts:62-63
Failure: `ageSeconds` is already divided by 1000, then compared with `NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS * 1000`. An empty result is therefore pinned for about 83 minutes. Verified: the listing was still empty 60 s after the source had rows, and recovered only past 5000 s. Only a permission change clears it; a newly created or shared document does not.
Fix: Compare in ms like `get` does: `this.clock.now() - entry.storedAt < NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS * 1000`.

5. Title: Cursor state is aliased and mutated, so reusing a cursor skips pages
Severity: P1
Location: api.ts:38-39 with cursor.ts:16 and cursor.ts:25
Failure: `resolveCursor` returns the stored `PageState` object. `list` then does `state.offset += items.length` on it and registers the same object under the new token. Every token in a chain points at one object whose offset keeps advancing. Verified: replaying the page-2 cursor returned rows from d20 instead of d10. A retry, a back navigation or two concurrent requests with one cursor silently skip data.
Fix: Never mutate resolved state. Issue `issueCursor({ query: state.query, offset: state.offset + items.length })`, and have `issueCursor` store its own copy.

## P2

6. Title: Cursor is not bound to the requesting viewer
Severity: P2 (P1 if tokens can reach another principal)
Location: api.ts:22-23, cursor.ts:15, cursor.ts:20-26
Failure: With a cursor, `request.viewerId`, `filter`, `sort` and `includeArchived` are ignored and the stored query runs. Verified: a request with `viewerId: "attacker"` and another viewer's cursor returned that viewer's documents. The token is a predictable counter plus 8 characters of `Math.random`, which is not a cryptographic source. This contradicts the comment at cursor.ts:8-9.
Fix: In `list`, reject when `state.query.viewerId !== request.viewerId`, and ideally when filter, sort or includeArchived differ. Generate tokens with `crypto.randomUUID()`.

7. Title: Negative and positive entries for a key are not mutually exclusive
Severity: P2 (latent until finding 4 is fixed)
Location: api.ts:73-79, cache.ts:48-57
Failure: Parallel State. `markEmpty` leaves the key's `fresh`/`stale` entry in place, and `set` leaves its `empty` entry in place. When a stale page revalidates to empty, the old rows stay in `stale`. Once the negative entry expires (5 s after the fix), `get` returns the old rows again as `stale`, and this repeats until the 150 s grace ends. Today the 5000 s negative TTL outlives the grace, which hides it.
Fix: Make `markEmpty` delete the key from `fresh` and `stale`, and `set` delete it from `empty`. Simpler: store `[]` as an ordinary entry with a per-entry TTL and remove the `empty` map.

8. Title: `pageSize` is not validated and `hasMore` is wrong at boundaries
Severity: P2
Location: api.ts:34-40
Failure: `items.length >= pageSize` is true for `pageSize <= 0`. Verified: `pageSize: 0` returns `hasMore: true` and a cursor whose offset never advances, so a client that follows cursors loops forever, leaking one cursor per call. NaN, negative and huge values also go straight to the source and into cache keys. Separately, when the total is an exact multiple of `pageSize`, the last full page reports `hasMore: true` and the client gets a trailing empty page.
Fix: Reject a non-integer or out-of-range `pageSize` at the top of `list`. For exact `hasMore`, fetch `pageSize + 1` rows and return `pageSize`.

9. Title: Background revalidation failure is an unhandled rejection
Severity: P2
Location: api.ts:67-70
Failure: `void fetch().then().finally()` has no rejection handler. A source error during revalidation becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which terminates the process under default Node and Bun settings.
Fix: Add a `.catch` that records the failure and keeps the stale entry, before `.finally`.

10. Title: Cursor store and cache maps grow without bound
Severity: P2
Location: cursor.ts:10 and cursor.ts:28-31; cache.ts:22-24
Failure: Dead Code Is Debt. `releaseCursor` has no caller and nothing expires cursors, although the error at cursor.ts:23 says "expired". Each non-final page adds a permanent entry to the module-global `live` map. Cache entries are evicted only when the same key is read again, and the keys contain client-controlled `filter`, `offset` and `pageSize`, so one-off queries accumulate forever in all three maps.
Fix: Give cursors a TTL or a size cap, or use a signed stateless cursor that encodes query and offset and delete the map. Add a size bound or periodic sweep to `SwrCache`.

11. Title: No tests for any of the new behaviour
Severity: P2
Location: api.ts, cache.ts, cursor.ts (no test files in the project)
Failure: `CacheClock` is injectable but unused by any test. Findings 1 to 5 would each fail a small fake-clock test.
Fix: Add behavioural tests for key isolation by `includeArchived`, invalidation across every tier including in-flight fetches, negative TTL expiry at 5 s, cursor replay returning the same page, and `hasMore` at exact and short pages.

## P3

12. Title: `:`-joined key is ambiguous
Severity: P3, UNVERIFIED (depends on the viewer-id alphabet, which is not in this project)
Location: api.ts:8, api.ts:84
Failure: If a viewer id can contain `:`, viewer `a:updated` with sort `title` and filter `f` gets the same key as viewer `a` with sort `updated` and filter `title:f`, which serves one viewer's page to another. `invalidatePrefix("a:")` also drops the other viewer's entries.
Fix: Encode the components, for example `JSON.stringify([viewerId, sort, filter, includeArchived, offset, pageSize])`, or hold a per-viewer map.

13. Title: `includeArchived` is not enforced, and the request type breaks callers
Severity: P3, UNVERIFIED (no callers or source implementation in this project)
Location: types.ts:15-17, api.ts:29
Failure: The field is documented as admin-only, but `list` forwards the client value unchecked. It is safe only if `DocumentSource` enforces the role. `page` was removed and `includeArchived` is a required boolean, so every existing caller fails to compile. `CacheClock.now()` (types.ts:39-41) does not state its unit, while cache.ts assumes ms.
Fix: Enforce or document where the admin check lives, make `includeArchived` optional with a `false` default, and document `now()` as epoch ms.

## Checked and found fine
- Deleting from a Map while iterating its keys in `invalidatePrefix` is safe in JS.
- The fresh and stale window arithmetic in `get` (cache.ts:32, cache.ts:40) is consistently in ms.
- The first-page state object is fresh per request, so the aliasing in finding 5 starts from the second page.",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings: (plan.md is not ready to implement; 4 P1, 4 P2, 2 P3. Read-only review; nothing run from the plan, since the snapshot holds only package.json, tests/unit/scripts/*, vscode/.vscodeignore and vscode/docs/*.)

1. Title: Phase 2 bumps web-tree-sitter to a version that does not exist and that @opentui/core forbids
Severity: P1
Location: plan.md phases[phase-2].tasks[t1] (description and all 3 test_scenarios); success_criteria[1]; implementation_contract d2
Failure: The plan calls 0.25.12 "the final patch release of the 0.25 line". The npm registry lists the 0.25 line as 0.25.0 through 0.25.10, then 0.26.0; `npm view web-tree-sitter@0.25.12` returns E404. The current pin 0.25.10 (package.json:107) is already the end of the line. Separately, package.json:85 says the hold exists "because @opentui/core pins that exact peer", and the registry confirms @opentui/core@0.5.1 has peerDependencies { web-tree-sitter: "0.25.10" }. Any move off 0.25.10 breaks the exact peer; the install fails outright on 0.25.12. Restating the note as "held at 0.25.12 because @opentui/core pins that exact peer" would make the note false, against the plan's own pattern "the note never lies".
Fix: Delete phase 2, success_criteria[1] and directive d2. Keep web-tree-sitter at 0.25.10 with the note unchanged.

2. Title: Phase 3 claims the .vsix ships vscode/docs; the packaging filter excludes releasing.md
Severity: P1
Location: plan.md summary ("release runbook that ships in the .vsix"); context.patterns[3]; phases[phase-3].tasks[t1] description and test_scenarios[1]; phase-3 qualitative_verification; success_criteria[3]; directive d3
Failure: vscode/.vscodeignore:7 ignores `docs/**`, and vscode/.vscodeignore:10 re-includes only `!docs/about-flywheel.md`; the comment at lines 8-9 calls it "the one docs file the extension opens at runtime". releasing.md is therefore not in the package. Scenario "inventory lists docs/releasing.md", the qualitative check, success criterion 4 and d3 cannot pass. The phase lists only vscode/docs/releasing.md as its file, so it does not change the filter either. The runbook is also maintainer content (Marketplace publisher access, PAT creation, `VSCE_PAT`, at vscode/docs/releasing.md:38-40,75), so adding `!docs/releasing.md` would be the wrong fix.
Fix: Drop every "ships in the .vsix / installed users read it" claim, context.patterns[3], success_criteria[3] and d3. Reframe phase 3 as a repository-only doc edit. Replace the package-inventory scenario with "the .vsix inventory still contains docs/about-flywheel.md and no other docs file".

3. Title: Baseline evidence cites a test file that does not exist
Severity: P1
Location: plan.md context.constraints[0]; context.key_files[1]; phases[phase-1].tasks[t1] ("extend the pin-ledger assertions"); phase-1 verification; success_criteria[4]; directive d1
Failure: tests/unit/scripts/dependency-pins.test.ts is absent. tests/unit/scripts holds 23 files, none with that name, and no test references "dependency-pins" or asserts on package.json pins. The claims "ran green on the unmodified tree", "one assertion per deliberate hold", "extends a proven contract, it does not create one" and "stays green ... as it was before the plan" are false. Phase 1 must create the ledger. As written, the phase-1 verification command only passes once the file is created, and the plan never says so.
Fix: Remove the baseline constraint. Restate t1 as creating the test file, and list the assertions it must hold (the @opentui lockstep; marked, web-tree-sitter and string-width/diff if they are treated as holds). Before adding a new file, check whether tests/unit/scripts/manifest.test.ts is the existing owner of manifest assertions; I did not read its contents.

4. Title: Phase 1 t1 raises a pin that is already at the target
Severity: P1
Location: plan.md context.key_files[0] ("@opentui/core is currently at 0.2.15 and must rise to 0.5.1"); phases[phase-1].tasks[t1] description; phase-1 goal
Failure: package.json:90 is `"@opentui/core": "0.5.1"` and package.json:91 is `"@opentui/solid": "0.5.1"`. The pins are already aligned, so the manifest edit is a no-op and the phase goal is already met. The premise misreads the staging test: tests/unit/scripts/binary-native-assets.test.ts:68 stages @opentui/core at 0.5.1, and line 73 stages the win32 native package at 0.2.15 as a deliberately stale fixture so that line 78 can expect its replacement with 0.5.1. "Already exercises the current 0.2.15" is wrong.
Fix: Remove the manifest raise and take binary-native-assets.test.ts out of the phase's file list; it must not be edited, because changing line 73 to 0.5.1 would make the replacement test vacuous. What remains of t1 is the lockstep ledger assertion only.

5. Title: The OpenAI SDK is a caret range, not an exact pin
Severity: P2
Location: plan.md context.key_files[0]; context.constraints[3]; phases[phase-1].tasks[t2] description and test_scenarios[2]; success_criteria[2]
Failure: package.json:102 is `"openai": "^6.39.0"`. The claims "already pinned exactly at 6.39.0" and "its resolution cannot drift between installs" are false; without a frozen lockfile it floats to any 6.x. Excluding it on that premise leaves the plan's stated reproducibility goal unmet for a runtime SDK. Success criterion 3 ("remains exactly 6.39.0 with no manifest edit") is unsatisfiable as worded.
Fix: Either pin openai to "6.39.0" in t2 with a ledger assertion, or record it as a deliberate, documented float. Correct the constraint and the success criterion either way.

6. Title: Phase 1 t2 has no defined scope and no test for what it changes
Severity: P2
Location: plan.md phases[phase-1].tasks[t2]
Failure: "Convert the floating runtime ranges the audit marks for exactness" names no packages, and no audit artifact exists in the plan or the snapshot. The floating runtime ranges are package.json:92 (@solid-primitives/keyed), 98 (fuzzysort), 99 (highlight.js), 100 (js-yaml), 102 (openai), 103 (partial-json) and 104 (sharp). All three scenarios assert only that things stay unchanged, so none can fail for a conversion that was done wrongly or not at all. This contradicts the plan's pattern "pin changes land with the ledger assertions that lock them". The plan also never names the lockfile, although constraints[5] implies the manifest phases regenerate it.
Fix: Enumerate each range to convert and its exact target version (the version the lockfile resolves today). Add a ledger assertion per conversion, or one "no caret in runtime dependencies except the documented floats" assertion. Add the lockfile to the phase's files. Note that sharp is staged at 0.35.3 in binary-native-assets.test.ts:69, which is a natural exact target.

7. Title: Verification commands do not prove the phases
Severity: P2
Location: plan.md phases[phase-2].verification; phases[phase-3].verification; phases[phase-2].tasks[t1].test_scenarios[2]
Failure: The phase-2 command runs opentui-native-package-patch.test.ts and binary-native-assets.test.ts. The first tests string rewriting of import shapes (tests/unit/scripts/opentui-native-package-patch.test.ts:8-74) and the second tests fixture packages in a temp dir (binary-native-assets.test.ts:59-83). Neither reads package.json or web-tree-sitter, so both pass regardless of the edit; the command also omits the ledger. The scenarios "fresh install resolves ..." and "note names ..." have no executing check. The phase-3 command `bun run package darwin-arm64` only builds; it does not list the inventory that d3 requires. It also yields a version-stamped file (the runbook shows `flywheel-darwin-arm64-0.0.1.vsix` at vscode/docs/releasing.md:10), which the plan never inspects.
Fix: Moot if findings 1 and 2 are accepted. Otherwise, verify with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` plus the ledger test, and with an inventory listing of the built .vsix (for example `bunx @vscode/vsce ls`).

8. Title: project_docs cites an AGENTS.md that is not in the snapshot
Severity: P2
Location: plan.md context.project_docs[0]
Failure: There is no AGENTS.md at the root or under vscode/ in this tree, so the implementer is pointed at a governing doc that cannot be read. UNVERIFIED: it may exist in the full repository outside this snapshot; the same applies to the scripts named in success_criteria[5] (scripts/test-parallel.ts, lint-parallel.ts, check-boundaries.ts), which package.json:17,54,75 declares but the snapshot omits.
Fix: Confirm the path in the full repository, or remove the entry.

9. Title: Proposed ledger scenarios duplicate each other and partly restate constants
Severity: P3
Location: plan.md phases[phase-1].tasks[t1].test_scenarios[0-1]; phases[phase-1].tasks[t2].test_scenarios[0-1]
Failure: Manual Sync. "Asserts one shared version" and "rejects a manifest where the two pins diverge" are the same assertion, unless the ledger exposes a pure checker that can be fed a divergent manifest, which the plan does not design. "marked stays exact at 17.0.1" restates a manifest constant. The real invariant comes from @opentui/core, whose registry metadata for 0.5.1 shows dependencies marked 17.0.1, diff 9.0.0, string-width 7.2.0 and peer web-tree-sitter 0.25.10, matching package.json:96,101,106,107.
Fix: Use one lockstep assertion. Where feasible, derive the held versions from node_modules/@opentui/core/package.json rather than hardcoding literals.

10. Title: The runbook the plan edits is stale about itself, and the plan's CI-ordering step already exists
